preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10^4) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip())
preconditions.description: All input lines are non-empty and properly formatted.

preconditions.expression: all(N.isdigit() and int(N) >= 2 and int(N) <= 2*10**5 for N in [line.split()[0] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line after T is an integer N (2 ≤ N ≤ 2*10^5) representing the number of vertices in the tree.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == N-1 for N, edges in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+N] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)]))
preconditions.description: Each test case has exactly N-1 edges, forming a tree.

preconditions.expression: all(all(u.isdigit() and v.isdigit() and 1 <= int(u) <= N and 1 <= int(v) <= N for u, v in [line.split() for line in edges]) for N, edges in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+N] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)]))
preconditions.description: Each edge (u_i, v_i) has 1 ≤ u_i, v_i ≤ N, where N is the number of vertices in the tree.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line.isdigit() and 0 <= int(output_line) <= N-2 for N, output_line in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()], [stdin.splitlines()[i+N+1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a single integer representing the minimum number of edges to add to the tree to form a Hamiltonian path, where 0 ≤ output ≤ N-2.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda edges: len(edges) == 0 or (lambda tree: any(len(leaves) == 1 for leaves in [leaf for leaf in tree if len(tree[leaf]) == 1]) or len([leaf for leaf in tree if len(tree[leaf]) == 1]) == 2))(build_tree(N, edges)) == (int(output_line) == 0) for N, edges, output_line in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+N] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)], [stdin.splitlines()[i+N+1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)]))
postconditions.description: If the tree already has a Hamiltonian path (i.e., it is a path graph or has exactly two leaves), the output is 0.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda edges: len(edges) > 0 and (lambda tree: len([leaf for leaf in tree if len(tree[leaf]) == 1]) == 2))(build_tree(N, edges)) == (int(output_line) == 1) for N, edges, output_line in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+N] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)], [stdin.splitlines()[i+N+1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)]))
postconditions.description: If the tree has exactly two leaves and is not already a path graph, the output is 1.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda edges: len(edges) > 0 and (lambda tree: len([leaf for leaf in tree if len(tree[leaf]) == 1]) == k))(build_tree(N, edges)) == (int(output_line) == k-2) for N, edges, output_line, k in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+N] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)], [stdin.splitlines()[i+N+1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)], [len([leaf for leaf in build_tree(N, edges) if len(build_tree(N, edges)[leaf]) == 1]) for N, edges in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+N] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)])]))
postconditions.description: If the tree has k leaves, the minimum number of edges to add to form a Hamiltonian path is k-2.
